window_relations.note: SECONDARY (2018-01-01..2025-09-01) is a strict SUPERSET of PRIMARY (2021-01-01..2025-09-01). Scoring a PRIMARY-SELECTED cell on SECONDARY is dilution-by-extra-years, NOT an out-of-sample check: the shrinkage it shows is expected under pure overfitting whether or not the effect is real. DISJOINT (2018-01-01..2021-01-01) = SECONDARY minus PRIMARY is the only genuinely held-out span in this pass. No permutation test and no max-of-correlated-normals correction was performed.

n_independent_position_paths.note: target-weight and drift-inclusive share ONE position path per (H,theta) -- they differ only in whether the drift re-trim is CHARGED -- while hold-shares is its own path (shares carried, weights drifting). So 48 cells rest on 32 distinct position paths, not 48. (Before the run-55 cycle-2 fix all three modes shared ONE path, i.e. 16.) Bonferroni-over-48 is KEPT: it controls FWER without any independence assumption, and is conservative here precisely because it re-tests each trajectory more than once.

cells_primary.cost_basis: target_change_only (Sum|d target|; drift assumed free) on the TARGET-WEIGHT book
upper_bound_unnetted (Sum|d target| + Sum|drift|; a triangle-inequality UPPER BOUND, per drift_retrim_turnover's own docstring) on the TARGET-WEIGHT book
hold_shares_actual (Sum|w_new - w_drifted|; the single netted trade) on the HOLD-SHARES book -- a DIFFERENT position path, not a different charge on the same one

renormalised_to_gross1.exact: the GROSS column is an EXACT rescaling of the realised return series (per-decision simple return is linear in the weights). It is NOT a book re-run under a gross-1 constraint: the holdings carried into the next decision are unrescaled. The net columns reuse the levered book's turnover and are an APPROXIMATION (which flatters this arm at 12 of 16 cells and penalises it at 4). No borrow column is emitted, so this arm is NOT stated in the pass's own gate quantity net21_borrow_low.

measured_correlation_primary_h1.note: rho MEASURED between each H=1 candidate's per-decision net21_borrow_low series and the H=1 frozen cell's, on the same 1704 rows. Cross-H cells cannot be paired (different n) and are less correlated in every measurable case here, hence have a LARGER MDE -- so the non-degenerate best below is a LOWER BOUND on the MDE of the cells the grid actually nominates.

raw_95pct.expected_false_positives_derivation: alpha/2 * n_cells, an UPPER BOUND (<=): the per-cell test is a TWO-SIDED 95% interval's lower bound clearing the band, i.e. one tail, so its null rate is at most 0.025 per cell -- attained only for a cell sitting exactly at the boundary null. Most cells sit far below the band and the 48 cells share position paths, so the true chance baseline is BELOW this figure. Reading it as an equality makes 'chance' easier to invoke than the data warrant.

uplift_ci_summary_primary.note: The band asks whether MAX uplift <= +0.20. A cell ANSWERS it only if its uplift CI lies wholly on one side of +0.20; a CI that STRADDLES +0.20 is undecided. The interval that may be read off a cell CHOSEN BY SEARCHING the grid is the Bonferroni one (alpha=0.05/48), not the raw 95%: any raw-95% clearance count at or below expected_false_positives_at_this_alpha is what chance alone produces over a 48-cell family and carries no verdict.

leverage_renormalisation.what_it_is: a PER-DECISION LEVERAGE-NEUTRAL RESCALING OF THE REALISED RETURN SERIES of the hold-shares book. Per-decision simple return is LINEAR in the weight vector, so dividing a decision's return by that decision's own Sum|w| is an EXACT rescaling of that return -- and not a uniform one, because Sum|w| varies (0.35..2.10 on PRIMARY, 0.2865..2.9185 across all three windows) and its variation is correlated with returns.
leverage_renormalisation.what_it_is_NOT: it is NOT 'the same book run at gross 1'. It never renormalises the HOLDINGS, so the drifted weights carried into the next decision are unchanged. A book actually constrained to gross_cap=1.0 renormalises its holdings each decision, after which the retrim rule mixes an UNSCALED target with a SCALED drift -- proportionality breaks and the position path diverges. See construction_caveat.
leverage_renormalisation.why_it_exists: cycle 2 recorded 'part of the hold-shares Sharpe advantage is a leverage/timing effect, not an accounting one, and this pass did not separate the two ... isolating them needs a new arm'. Isolating the leverage component needs no new arm (hold_shares_walk already returns held_w). What the measurement then delivers is a bound, not a verdict: see verdict / construction_caveat.

summary_primary.verdict: UNRESOLVED. De-levering removes ~85% of the full-window hold-shares gross advantage over target-weight and leaves a residue an order of magnitude inside this design's SE. That is what is measured. It is NOT a demonstration that the advantage IS entirely gross-exposure scaling: the residue's sign is construction-dependent (see construction_caveat) and NEITHER construction's paired CI clears zero. The raw advantage itself does not clear zero either (+0.2794, 95% CI [-0.088, +0.638] at the frozen cell), so no promotion is supported under any construction.

construction_caveat.what_this_module_ships: the proxy ret/G -- a rescaling of the REALISED return series, holdings unchanged.
construction_caveat.the_alternative: a book genuinely constrained to gross_cap=1.0, which renormalises its HOLDINGS each decision (w /= Sum|w| after the retrim mix) and therefore carries different weights into the next decision.
construction_caveat.transcribed_from: a cycle-3 estimator lens BUILT that constrained book on the same walk and validated it (Sum|w| = 1 +/- 4e-16, r = Sum w_i r_i to 4.4e-16, identical asset support). This closing pass TRANSCRIBES that lens's figures; it did NOT rebuild the book.
construction_caveat.conclusion: the two constructions give OPPOSITE sign patterns and NEITHER clears zero. The leverage question is UNRESOLVED at this design's power, and 'no consistent sign' is a property of the proxy, not of the mode. Rebuilding the constrained book inside this harness is follow-up work.

gate_quantity_caveat.problem: renormalised_to_gross1 emits gross + net8/12/21 and NO borrow, while every band / uplift / significance / candidate statement in this pass is denominated in net21_borrow_low. The de-levering conclusion is argued in gross and net21, NOT in the gate quantity (D81(c)).
gate_quantity_caveat.transcribed_arm: a cycle-3 flow verifier re-denominated it properly -- weights held_w/G, turnover turn/G, borrow charged on the DE-LEVERED short notional -- and got renorm minus target-weight of -0.0380 .. +0.0497 with 9 of 16 cells positive: the same 'no consistent sign', the same order-of-magnitude collapse. The conclusion HOLDS in the gate quantity; it was simply never demonstrated there.
gate_quantity_caveat.note: in the gate quantity the RAW advantage is LARGER (+0.2282 .. +0.3260 vs the +0.1012 .. +0.2923 quoted on gross) because the hold-shares book carries less short notional and so pays less borrow.
gate_quantity_caveat.status: the borrow column is NOT added here -- that is new computation. Rowed as follow-up work.

bear22_counter_check.reading: renormalisation does NOT rescue hold-shares in BEAR22 -- the de-levered book loses to target-weight there by MORE than the levered one does (-0.775 vs -0.602). So Correction 2's BEAR22 DIRECTION is a genuine compositional effect and SURVIVES this correction, while the full-window ADVANTAGE is left UNRESOLVED (see summary_primary.verdict and construction_caveat) rather than killed. Note the two windows are NOT the same mechanism read twice: in the full window the exposure drift accounts for ~85% of the effect, whereas in BEAR22 it was mildly CUSHIONING a deficit that comes from elsewhere (mostly the compounding convention, per correction 2's attribution) and that survives its removal. That asymmetry is measured, not assumed.
bear22_counter_check.direction_support: the BEAR22 direction rests on the RENORMALISED gap (-0.7750, paired 95% CI [-1.109, -0.452], stable across 6 bootstrap seeds) plus the 830_corridor prior -- NOT on the total gap. The TOTAL gap -0.6019 has paired 95% CI [-1.158, -0.037] at the shipped seed but [-1.115, +0.009] at seed 3, i.e. it straddles zero on another draw. Both CIs transcribed from the cycle-3 estimator lens; not recomputed here.

leverage_renormalisation.cost_caveat: GROSS columns are an EXACT rescaling of the realised return series. NET columns charge the LEVERED book's own turnover against the de-levered return series (a book actually run at gross 1 would trade different notionals), so they are an approximation. DIRECTION, corrected in the closing pass: it flatters the renormalised arm at 12 of 16 PRIMARY cells and PENALISES it at 4 -- mean Sum|w| exceeds 1 at H=2/th=1.0 (1.0142), H=3/th=1.0 (1.0104) and H=5/th=1.0 (1.0316), and at H=1/th=1.0 (mean 0.9931) the per-cell recomputation still penalises, because Sharpe depends on G's whole distribution and not on its mean. Cycle 3's 'mean Sum|w| < 1 at EVERY cell, so the net columns flatter this arm' was a FALSE universal, contradicted by this module's own hold_shares_diag. Magnitude <= 0.002 Sharpe, so nothing flips (max RENORM-TW +0.0309 -> +0.0303, min -0.0429 -> -0.0442); the gross-only comparison carries the conclusion regardless.

correction_4_theta_flip_reduction.record_claim: tactics_gaps.md:43 (self-labelled heuristic, 'must be measured'): 'theta = 0.5 sigma kills 40-50% of flips', '~70-75%' at theta=1 sigma
correction_4_theta_flip_reduction.verdict: the record UNDERSTATES hysteresis in the permissive direction -- theta=0.5 removes far more flip turnover than 40-50%. So theta is NOT the cheap free lunch the record implies: it cuts deep enough to destroy signal, which is exactly what the high-theta cells' strongly negative Delta net shows.

band_disposition.reason: Three independent instruments agree. (1) MDE: the design's minimum detectable uplift at 80% power is 1.6x-13x the pre-registered +-0.20 band across every correlation assumption, including the most favourable one MEASURED on this panel (mde_primary, measured_correlation_primary_h1). (2) DIRECT: a block-bootstrap CI on the UPLIFT ITSELF -- paired where the rows allow it -- straddles +0.20 for 46 of 48 cells at the family's own pre-registered alpha=0.05/48, and 0 of 48 cells clear the band at that alpha on ANY of the three windows (uplift_ci_summary_*). The grid's own max-uplift cell is among the undecided. (3) HOLDOUT: on the genuinely disjoint 2018-2020 window, 0/48 cells' uplift CI even excludes zero. This conclusion is PRIOR TO and INDEPENDENT OF the hold-shares implementation -- no re-implementation rescues it.
band_disposition.what_would_resolve_it: roughly 30x more decisions at this SE (SE scales as 1/sqrt(n), so shrinking a 0.46 SE to the ~0.05 needed to resolve +-0.20 at Bonferroni alpha needs ~85x the sample), or a paired design that shares decision rows across the whole grid (the H axis structurally cannot), or a pre-registered SINGLE cell instead of a 48-cell search.
band_disposition.precedent: same disposition run 54 gave TASK_917's P1 (kill refused for want of power -> D84).
